title: Public-Records Due Diligence: Check a Supplier, Buyer or Partner Before You Commit
tagline: A calm, repeatable way to check who you are about to sign with, using public records only.
audience: Small business owners about to sign with a new supplier, buyer or partner
Office managers and bookkeepers who approve new suppliers or payment details
Small procurement and operations teams with no legal department
outcomes: Write a clear scope for a supplier, buyer or partner check
Work through a source ladder of free public registers and records
Record every finding with its source, date and confidence
Tell red flags from noise and turn flags into polite questions
Write a defensible one-page pre-read for a decision maker
Work ethically and know when to stop and call a lawyer or accountant

questions.q: What should you write down before you start searching?
options: The counterparty, the decision, the exposure and the depth
Only the counterparty's website address
A list of every registry in Australia
Nothing until you find something worrying
questions.why: A scope keeps the check focused and shows you had a legitimate business purpose.

questions.q: An observed finding is one that...
options: Is your best guess about what a record means
You saw directly in a public source and can point to
Someone told you by phone
Appears in a news headline only
questions.why: Observed means directly seen in a source. Your reading of it is inferred.

questions.q: ABN Lookup shows an ABN as cancelled, but the supplier is still trading. What is the best response?
options: Report them as dishonest
Ignore it because ABNs do not matter
Record it and ask which entity you are contracting with
Stop all contact permanently
questions.why: A mismatch is a question for them. There may be an ordinary explanation, and their answer is useful information.

questions.q: Which statement is written the safest way?
options: The company is hiding debts
The ASIC register showed the company status as deregistered on the date searched
The directors are crooks
They are clearly going under
questions.why: State what the source showed, with the date. Avoid conclusions about character.

questions.q: A court judgment search returns nothing. What does that tell you?
options: The organisation is clean
The organisation is in trouble
Only that nothing was found on the sites searched on that day
The search tool is broken
questions.why: Blank results are worth recording, but not every matter is published, so they do not prove a clean record.

questions.q: A PPSR registration from a lender appears against a supplier. Usually this is...
options: Proof of fraud
Routine business finance, so often noise
A reason to cancel the order
A sign the ABN is invalid
questions.why: Security interests are common in ordinary trading. Consider them where goods you pay for might be affected.

questions.q: You find a possible match on the DFAT consolidated list. What should you do?
options: Decide yourself whether it is the same party
Confront the other party
Stop, record what you saw and get advice from a lawyer
Delete the notes
questions.why: Names can be similar and dealing with a listed party is serious. This is a clear stop point.

questions.q: A supplier's domain has no DMARC policy. How should you treat this?
options: As proof they are dishonest
As an observed security gap, and confirm bank detail changes by phone
As a reason to scan their servers
As irrelevant to payments
questions.why: Weak email posture makes impersonation easier. Record it fairly and protect your payment process.

questions.q: Which action stays inside this method?
options: Testing their website login forms
Calling their staff pretending to be a customer
Looking up their SPF and DMARC records with a public DNS lookup
Scanning their servers for open ports
questions.why: Public lookups are reading records. The other options touch systems or involve impersonation.

questions.q: Which is most likely a real red flag rather than noise?
options: A new company with no other warning sign
One old, resolved dispute
A published liquidator appointment just before you plan to pay a deposit
Absence from AusTender for a supplier that never claimed government work
questions.why: Insolvency notices bear directly on money you are about to pay. The others are usually ordinary.

questions.q: What belongs in section 5 of the one-page pre-read?
options: What you could not check
Your opinion of the directors
The registry fees
A draft contract
questions.why: Honest gaps keep the reader from assuming the check covered more than it did.

questions.q: Where should you share a pre-read that names real people?
options: In an industry chat group
On social media
Only with people who need it for the decision, stored securely
With the other organisation's competitors
questions.why: Limiting circulation protects privacy and reduces the risk of defaming anyone.
